summary.text: Kedner Maxime, a Haitian-born accountant, immigration consultant and pastor, ran as the Independent Party of Florida nominee and lost the November 3, 2026 election for Florida's 20th Congressional District to Debbie Wasserman Schultz.
He was born and raised in Port-de-Paix, Haiti, came to the United States in 1981 and has been a pastor for 16 years.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, Maxime was born and raised in Port-de-Paix, Haiti, and came to the United States in April 1981, at age 18, as a student.
He says his first jobs in this country were washing dishes and mowing golf courses, and that he sometimes worked three jobs at once.

His campaign website says he completed a GED at Dillard High School, an associate degree in business administration at Broward College and a bachelor's degree in business administration at Nova Southeastern University. He was ordained in 2011 with a Master of Theology and holds a Doctor of Divinity from Liberty Bible School & Seminary.
Maxime founded Advantage Tax Firm Consulting Services in 1996, where he says he works as an accountant and immigration consultant.
He says he has been a pastor for 16 years at L'Eglise la Voix du Salut and has hosted the Tass Cafe Show on WLQY 1320AM for 20 years.
He advanced to the general election as the Independent Party of Florida nominee after that party's August 18, 2026 primary was canceled.
His campaign website listed issue pages on costs, immigration, healthcare and education.
He received 3.9% of the vote to Debbie Wasserman Schultz's 74.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
His campaign website says he married in 1984 and has two children and a granddaughter.
